title: AI Is Driving Up Treasury Yields: ‘It Just Touches Everything’
summary:
There are no signs that the AI debt deluge is slowing.
That has allowed him to keep the size of 10-year and 30-year bond sales steady.
But in a note to clients on Friday, Bank of America Corp.'s economists said the AI borrowing is "potentially crowding out long-end Treasury demand" and has played a major role in the rise of bond yields.
That is likely problematic for the Treasury, according to Jonathan Cohn, head of US rates desk strategy at Nomura.
A growing supply of long-dated debt from AI-related companies could force the Treasury to reduce the size of its own long-term debt sales to avoid higher borrowing costs.

title: Alina Kukarina on why AI transformation begins before choosing the technology
summary:
Her experience across digital transformation, software, and management training has led her to examine how organizations make decisions before technology enters the picture.
Organizations need to understand how work happens, where value is created or lost, and where human judgment remains essential before assigning technology a role,” she states.
Technology identifies which technology to choose and whether AI will provide meaningful assistance.

summary:

Gundlach compared the idea to issuing 30-year asset-backed securities against warehouses of bananas, even if they were "newly engineered bananas of unknown life."
It’s OK, they’ll be newly engineered bananas of unknown life.
Gundlach's argument largely centered on a mismatch between the debt's duration and how long the chips remain valuable.

title: AI Boom Has Echoes of Enron but Isn't Doomed to Crash, Tech Guru Says
summary:
Today's tech titans are using similar financial tactics to Enron, but that doesn't mean they're careening toward disaster, one AI guru says.
"The AI buildout is replicating versions of all three, entirely legally, and that is exactly why it deserves attention," said the coauthor of "The AI-Centered Enterprise," and the cofounder and chief product and AI officer of an AI startup named Samvid.
He described how private equity firms including KKR are helping to finance the AI buildout.
Fragile forecastsAs for demand projections, Bala said the current buildout is being "financed against demand curves that are marked to model, not to market."
An example from a consumer's perspective might be leasing a car using financing from the car's manufacturer.

title: Alphabet takes its AI debt spree Down Under with a first Australian dollar bond
summary:
Alphabet is preparing to sell its first bond denominated in Australian dollars, a modest-sounding piece of financial housekeeping that says a good deal about how the AI build-out is now being paid for.
Only weeks ago Alphabet raised US$25bn in a twice-yearly dollar bond to bankroll its AI expansion, and in June it topped that up with an equity raise of around $85bn.
Alphabet has been doing precisely that, having also lined up a debut yen bond earlier in the same funding spree.
“Not only is it Alphabet’s first-ever Australian dollar bond, but it’s also the first AI hyperscaler to access the Australian dollar market,” noted Chamath De Silva of BetaShares, and the deal would comfortably eclipse the roughly $2.25bn Apple sold in Australia more than a decade ago.
The Australian bond is a small chapter in that larger book, but a revealing one.

title: The Powerful Chinese AI Model Experts Warned About Is Here
summary:
Last Friday, the Chinese AI company Z.ai announced a powerful open-weight model that it says is capable of automating cutting-edge coding and cybersecurity tasks almost as well as the best publicly available models from Anthropic and OpenAI.
The new model, GLM 5.3, could be a gift for companies looking to secure their systems against attacks, providing a cheaper way to scan for hidden bugs and other weaknesses.
Alongside the new model, Z.ai released OpenVuln, a service for scanning code repositories for vulnerabilities using GLM 5.3.
Like Anthropic, OpenAI has made its most advanced models available to a limited number of partners prior to full release.
Some believe that open-source AI will be crucial to shoring systems up from attack; Nvidia recently announced an alliance to promote the use of open AI for cybersecurity.

title: Azerbaijan wants to become a tech hub as its startups raised $2.6m last year
summary:
Every petrostate eventually discovers that the oil will not last forever, and Azerbaijan has reached the stage of the story where the government starts talking about technology.
Twenty-two startups raised a combined $2.62 million in 2025, a figure that a single mid-sized seed round in Berlin or London would swallow whole.
Three local funds, Caucasus Ventures, INMerge Ventures, and Tumar Ventures, hold around $11 million in disclosed capital between them.
Officials cite Singapore and Estonia as the models they have in mind, and they would like Baku to become the technology hub of the Caspian.
TNW’s own dispatch from Kazakhstan’s tech scene found a market several steps down the road Baku is only now setting out on.

title: Anthropic explains how Claude’s invisible text watermarks will work
summary:
Take the sentence “The weather today was cold and…”.
Watermarking uses low-stakes choices like these—which occur many times over a piece of generated text—to leave a pattern in Claude’s responses.
That pattern is undetectable to the reader, but is detectable to anyone who has a key that encodes it.
When watermarking is used, choices are still made at random, but the source of the randomness is different.
Instead of using an arbitrary random number generator to pick the next word, watermarking uses the key and a few words that come before to settle what word the model should pick.

title: Becoming AI-Native Requires the Right People More Than the Right Technology. Here’s the Shift Leaders Need to Make.
summary:
AI adoption is primarily a people challenge, requiring structured experimentation, change management, and new hybrid roles that connect technical capabilities with business needs.
The companies that become AI-native will not be the ones with the longest list of AI tools.
AI adoption is a people challenge firstThere is a persistent misconception that access to AI technology equals transformation.
Human judgment becomes more valuableAs organizations become AI-native, AI shifts from supporting individual solutions to powering shared, repeatable systems, and the leverage compounds.
It is not a limitation to design around but the mechanism that makes AI workflows trustworthy enough to scale.

summary:

Nvidia’s own credit default swaps hit a record after it announced $750bn of AI deals, which is the market pricing the same worry rather than tweeting about it.
It is not whether AI works, but whether a graphics processor is still worth lending against in year seven.

title: Groq closes $350M Series A at $3.5bn evaluation and Nvidia joins the round
summary:
Groq, the AI-inference chip company that spent the better part of a decade pitching itself as the scrappy alternative to Nvidia, has raised fresh money at a valuation that quietly concedes how much has changed.
The company announced on Monday that they took in $350m at a $3.5bn valuation, roughly half the $6.9bn it commanded last September.
The round was led by Disruptive, the Dallas firm whose founder Alex Davis is now Groq’s executive chairman, and, in a twist that would be difficult to invent, Nvidia itself joined in.
A $650m raise in June was the opening act of that reconstruction, and this $350m round is the second.
Backing Groq costs Nvidia very little, and it buys a friendly, dependent supplier of inference capacity, plus a stake in whatever the rebuilt firm turns out to be.

title: Apple Fitness+ could be getting live sessions, but probably not
summary:
An Apple job listing appears to be suggesting that the company might be planning some live Apple Fitness+ sessions.
If you thrive in a fast-paced, ever-evolving environment and want to be part of a collaborative, innovative team redefining live production at Apple, this is your chance.
Understanding of both live production and post production, and can seamlessly bounce back and forth between the two worldsMust be comfortable in a control room, in an office environment, and on a live setHowever, it’s hard to see any benefit of live Fitness+ sessions over pre-recorded ones.
At most, I could envisage some kind of real-time events on special occasions, but I would still expect the actual fitness sessions to be pre-recorded.

title: Norway Should Buy OpenAI
summary:
They are trained on vast quantities of text, images, and code scraped from the internet and digitized archives.
Clearly, the most transformative technology since agriculture should not be left in private hands.
Thus, the Norwegian Government Pension Fund Global ought to purchase OpenAI and manage it for the benefit of the international community.
Formerly, OpenAI was a non-profit, with capped profits and a windfall clause guaranteeing an intelligence explosion would benefit all of humanity.
With the capital of Norwegian Social-Democracy, we can return the lab to public hands.

title: Europe’s defence-AI champion Helsing is using Rakuten to break into Japan’s arms market
summary:
Helsing, the Munich startup that has become Europe’s best-funded defence-AI company, is pushing into Asia, and it has found an unlikely guide.
At the centre of the effort is the HX-2, a compact AI-guided strike drone that Japan’s military is putting through field trials due to run until the end of September.
Japan’s own trials, with another month left to run, will be watched closely for exactly that reason.
Helsing has been building an AI submarine, striking an alliance with Mistral on military AI, and casting itself as a pillar of Europe’s scramble to rearm.
Selling into Asia extends that ambition well beyond NATO, and quietly turns a European champion into a would-be global arms supplier.
